claim_verdicts.evidence: refs kustomization.md: "Since 1.14, kubectl also supports the management of Kubernetes objects using a kustomization file. To view resources found in a directory containing a kustomization file, run the following command: kubectl kustomize <kustomization_directory>". kubectl.docs Kustomize intro (WebFetch): "Kustomize provides a solution for customizing Kubernetes resource configuration free from templates and DSLs."

Claim reworded in round 2 to drop 'without contacting a cluster'. refs kustomization.md: "To view resources found in a directory containing a kustomization file, run the following command: kubectl kustomize <kustomization_directory>"; line 21: "To apply those resources, run `kubectl apply` with `--kustomize` or `-k` flag". Viewing and applying are separate commands.

refs kustomization.md: "A base is a directory with a kustomization.yaml, which contains a set of resources and associated customization." "The kustomization.yaml in an overlay directory may refer to multiple bases, combining all the resources defined in these bases into a unified configuration. Additionally, it can apply customizations on top of these resources"; example overlays use "resources: - ../base".

Round 2: claim now says a target selects one or several objects. refs kustomization.md: "`patches` may be a file or an inline string, targeting a single or multiple resources." "The patch target selects resources by group, version, kind, name, namespace, labelSelector and annotationSelector." Json6902 example "- op: replace / path: /spec/replicas / value: 3" -> "replicas: 3"; page shows strategic-merge and Json6902 forms. Recorded diff: only replicas 2 vs 3.

refs feature list: "images ... Each entry is to modify the name, tags and/or digest for one image without creating patches". kubectl.docs images page (WebFetch, round 1): "Apply will override the images whose image name matches name with a new tag." Repo stage-3: base/api.yaml and base/migrate-hook.yaml use untagged donhang-api / donhang-migrate; each overlay has a separate images entry for each, as the claim now says.

refs kustomization.md: "To use a generated ConfigMap in a Deployment, reference it by the name of the configMapGenerator. Kustomize will automatically replace this name with the generated name." "The generated ConfigMaps and Secrets have a content hash suffix appended. This ensures that a new ConfigMap or Secret is generated when the contents are changed." Recorded run: "2 name: api-..." (ConfigMap + envFrom).

refs deployment.md: "A Deployment's rollout is triggered if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (that is, .spec.template) is changed". base/api.yaml at stage-3: envFrom configMapRef name: api sits under spec.template.spec.containers, so the rewritten generated name changes .spec.template.

refs kustomization.md: "To disable the behavior of appending a suffix, one can use generatorOptions" with "disableNameSuffixHash: true". refs configmap.md: "ConfigMaps consumed as environment variables are not updated automatically and require a pod restart." With a stable name the Pod template is unchanged, so no rollout (deployment.md line 167).

issues.text: Section 4 says each overlay's `images` entry holds what *this* environment runs, so I expect the diff to show image lines too. The prose explains their absence with "both overlays now name the same images", but "now" points to a moment the lesson never described; only a code comment hints that production runs what staging runs.
issues.quote: only the replica count, because both overlays now name the same images.
issues.fix: Replace with "only the replica count, because at this tag staging's `images` entries name the same tag and digest as production's".

issues.text: The second paragraph after the output still does four things: the two `api-` names, `api-egress`, where the ConfigMap comes from, and the diff. The `configMapGenerator` sentence sits between the name explanation and the diff, so I had to re-read to see which part of the output each sentence matches.
